_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-6 (Seafood) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). Numbers come from data/standards/seafood-compiled/<record>.json (deterministic; no authored values). This file carries display + wiring + the category _meta block only.

_meta.tier_footnote: Mercury is limited in both forms: total mercury (tHg) and methylmercury (MeHg) are separate ceilings that must both be met. Total arsenic (tAs) operates as a reflex screen to inorganic-arsenic (iAs) speciation, since most arsenic in seafood is non-toxic organic arsenobetaine. Tin (Sn) is material only for canned product, where it migrates from the can; for non-canned seafood it is controlled by screen, not limited.
_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — government-limit default (CLAUDE.md Part 19, Governing Principles v2.0)
_meta.manual_method_note: Seafood limits are taken at face value in each product’s native basis; there is no reconstitution conversion. Mercury is limited in both forms — total mercury (Hg) and methylmercury (MeHg) are separate ceilings, set to the species-specific tier each government assigns (predatory fish carry the higher ceiling, lower-trophic species the lower). Tier 1 toxics (Pb, Cd, iAs, Hg) are zero-tolerance; Tier 2 (tAs, Sn) carry the program’s 150% transitional allowance. Total arsenic operates as a reflex screen to inorganic-arsenic speciation. Tin is material only for canned product, where it migrates from the can; for non-canned seafood it is controlled by screen, not assigned an invented number.

pages.name: Marine predatory fish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for marine predatory fish — tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish — stated as consumed (edible portion, wet weight). Predatory species carry the higher species-specific mercury ceiling every government sets for them; every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for the product, with a disclosed read-across where none regulates the exact analyte.

pages.name: Marine non-predatory fish (sardine, anchovy, salmon, cod, herring, mackerel)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for marine non-predatory fish — sardine, anchovy, salmon, cod, herring, mackerel — as fillet or muscle meat, fresh or frozen, stated as consumed. These lower-trophic species carry the lower government mercury ceiling; every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for the product.

pages.name: Freshwater fish (tilapia, catfish, trout, carp)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for freshwater finfish — tilapia, catfish, trout, carp — stated as consumed. Trout is in the lower-mercury government group, which binds the subcategory mercury ceiling; every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for the product.

pages.name: Shellfish (crustaceans and bivalve molluscs)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for shellfish — crustaceans (shrimp, crab, lobster) and bivalve molluscs (mussels, clams, oysters, scallops) — not canned, stated as consumed. Bivalves concentrate cadmium, and the cadmium ceiling reflects the strictest applicable government maximum; every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for the product.

pages.name: Cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for cephalopods — octopus, squid, cuttlefish — not canned, stated as consumed. Cephalopods carry the strictest inorganic-arsenic ceiling in all of seafood (EU 2025/1891, 50 ppb); every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for the product, with a disclosed read-across for methylmercury where none regulates it.

pages.name: Seaweed & kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for seaweed and kelp foods — nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, stated as sold. Seaweed concentrates arsenic and heavy metals on drying, and the ceilings reflect the strictest government maximum for the dried product form; every limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for dried seaweed.

pages.name: Canned seafood (canned tuna, canned fish)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for canned seafood — canned tuna and canned fish — stated as consumed. The metal ceilings are the general-fish government floor; the tin ceiling reflects the strictest canned-fishery maximum, because tin migrates from the can. A species-identified canned product (for example canned salmon) additionally meets its species subcategory where stricter.
